findings.text: 72 chemotype(s); the largest holds 108 of 244 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 6 heavy atoms, about 32% of a typical molecule, and 95% of the set can be cut at it

the 6 shared framework atoms sit 2.9 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (244 of 244 carry them); but that framework is only 32% of a typical molecule and matches it 24 ways on average, so this cannot say whether the set shares a frame -- look at it
the chosen attenuation 5 is at the top of the grid: the search needed a value it was not offered, so widen it before believing the model

the descriptor baseline reproduces the activity almost exactly (q2 +0.965); on a set this size that is not chemistry but the measurement itself, reached through the file's own columns -- the nearest are mwila_hcl_adj (r 0.83), mwila_pooled_adj (r 0.82), calc:clogp (r 0.32), mw (r 0.31). No descriptor conclusion can be drawn until they are excluded.
dropped from the descriptor baseline because they reproduce the activity rather than describe the molecule: mwila_pooled_raw -- if one of these is a real descriptor, name it and run again
the aligned model is -0.109 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.220 to +0.012) -- the frame gains nothing over counts
the aligned model is +0.016 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.097 to +0.136) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -0.077 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.204 to +0.043) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is -0.633 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval -0.758 to -0.530) -- descriptors alone do as well, so the geometry adds nothing on this set

why: the frame gains nothing over counts, which needs no alignment to curate and cannot be done wrongly
